hero.text: I'm Adiel Soares, a Product Designer with a strong background in Frontend Engineering. I work from defining the experience to implementing the interface, connecting user needs, product decisions and technical quality.

about.title: From strategy to interfaces in production.
about.p1: I have been working on digital products since 2017. I started out building systems and interfaces and, over time, took a growing part in product decisions: understanding the problem, structuring information, designing interactions and following implementation through.
about.p2: Today I work as a Senior UX/UI Designer. My engineering background helps me propose solutions that make sense for the people using them, for the organization's goals and for the team that will build and maintain the product.
about.p3: I have worked at G4F, Capgemini, IBTI and Aparece Brasil, on projects for public organizations and private companies. Much of that work involved institutional systems, administrative workflows and interfaces that must follow consistent standards.

strategy.context: Digital products start with questions: who uses them, what they need to solve and what the business expects to achieve. At this stage, the work is about reducing uncertainty before designing screens.
challenges: Legacy flows that grew without planning
Extensive content with no clear hierarchy
strategy.ux: Understand the problem before proposing solutions, and document decisions so the team knows why each flow exists.
strategy.engineering: Assess technical feasibility early, considering integrations, business rules and data constraints during discovery.

designSystems.context: Interfaces that grow without patterns accumulate inconsistencies. A Design System organizes visual and interaction decisions so the product can evolve coherently.
challenges: A gap between what is designed and what is built
Accessibility addressed only at the end
designSystems.ux: Predictable patterns reduce cognitive load: people learn the interface once and reuse that knowledge.
designSystems.engineering: Tokens and components need a counterpart in code. Shared naming between design and frontend reduces rework.

frontend.context: The quality of an interface also depends on how it is built. During implementation, design decisions become structure, behavior and performance.
challenges: Loss of fidelity between prototype and production
Tightly coupled components that are hard to maintain
Layouts that break at intermediate screen sizes
frontend.ux: Responsiveness, loading states and immediate feedback are part of the experience, not finishing touches.
frontend.engineering: Readable code and small components make maintenance, testing and product evolution easier.

enterprise.context: Institutional and enterprise systems often combine complex rules, different access profiles and long administrative workflows. A clear interface reduces errors and makes work more predictable.
challenges: Long forms and complex validation rules
A need for consistency across systems
enterprise.ux: In complex environments, the interface should show the status of each process and make the next action clear.
enterprise.engineering: Standardized components and centralized rules help keep modules and teams consistent.
